captions.detailed: A Japanese bonshō temple bell suspended from a heavy timber post-and-beam hanging frame. The structure features a large, straight-sided bronze bell hanging from the top crossbeam, designed to rotate slightly on a revolute joint at its crown pin. A cylindrical log striker is mounted to a pivot arm on one of the frame posts, allowing it to swing on a revolute joint to strike the side of the bell.
captions.instruction: Create an articulated 3D model of a Japanese bonshō temple bell hanging from a heavy wooden post-and-beam frame. The assembly must include a revolute joint connecting the bell to the upper crossbeam, and a separate revolute joint for a wooden log striker pivot-mounted to one of the vertical posts so it can swing and strike the bell.
captions.factory: Construct the support frame using Box primitives to form the vertical posts, base plates, crossbeams, and diagonal corner braces. Model the bell by revolving a 2D profile or lofting concentric circles to create its flared cylindrical shape. Create the striker as a Cylinder primitive, and attach it to a pivot arm made from a Box. Define two revolute joints: one at the top of the bell connecting it to the crossbeam, and another at the striker's pivot pin on the side post.
